summary: Margaret Killjoy recounts the socialist, Catholic, republican and anarchist plotters who tried to assassinate Benito Mussolini in Italy between 1921 and 1932, from Violet Gibson to Gino Lucetti, and the trials and executions that followed.

evidence.note: Robert introduces two republished Cool People Who Did Cool Stuff episodes
1898 food riot massacre motivates Bresci, who kills King Umberto I in 1900
first known plot against Mussolini, by anarchists in 1921, betrayed by Masi
last attempt covered: Sbardellotto in Rome in 1932, tried and shot
Lucetti dies in prison during a 1943 air raid; partisan units named after him
Bresci lives in Paterson, New Jersey, before returning to Italy
Italian refugee popular front in France plans the Lucetti attempt
Schirru leaves New York, makes bombs in Belgium, goes to Rome
Bibbi and later Tommasini fight in the Spanish Civil War
fascists exploit the Sacco and Vanzetti case for nationalist propaganda
New York Times coverage flatters Mussolini after the Zamboni attempt
crowd stabs fifteen-year-old Anteo Zamboni to death

notes: Republished Cool People Who Did Cool Stuff two-parter; hero chosen over crossover by format precedence. Primary subject is the set of attempts (event), so no roles and no lifetime rule; Mussolini is secondary. Schirru gets a segment comparable to Bresci but the subject cap is five. Covered span ends 1943 (Lucetti's death, Zaniboni's release); later epilogues of Gibson, Bibbi and Tommasini are brief. Terrorism primary because assassination is the pitch; fascism-far-right is close.
